description: Brass wheels turn slowly above a floor of dark stone, each carrying a small flag that says PLEASE TAKE YOUR TIME. The Metronome Golem tends a loom that makes symbols visible one sample at a time. A Chameleon occupies the negotiation console, trying to match two lists without becoming a third list. Across the gallery, a Red Scorpion demonstrates an infrared aperture. The symbol plinth, sampling gate and notebook table form an untimed circuit you may pause or replay freely. The path back to the workshop stays open; the guarded corridor toward the Backhoe Rift explains its preparation requirements before you enter.

hotspots.label: Master timing wheel
hotspots.description: The wheel has all day. Its flags read “Pause whenever useful” and “There is no timing score.” Observe the sampling marks at your own pace; no rhythmic keypress opens the corridor.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: That will not help with this exhibit. Look at its readable labels, or choose one of its offered actions; every useful interaction has a keyboard-accessible control.

hotspots.label: Four-level signal plinth
hotspots.description: Read the complete teaching map: −3→00, −1→01, +1→10, +3→11. These are toy levels, not volts. Do not replace this map with a remembered real-PHY coding scheme.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: That will not help with this exhibit. Look at its readable labels, or choose one of its offered actions; every useful interaction has a keyboard-accessible control.

hotspots.label: Sampling gate
hotspots.description: Four windows are labeled in order: position 0 shows −3; 1 shows +1; 2 shows +3; 3 shows −1. Inspect each window freely. Their order matters; how quickly you read them does not.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: That will not help with this exhibit. Look at its readable labels, or choose one of its offered actions; every useful interaction has a keyboard-accessible control.

hotspots.label: Clock-recovery model
hotspots.description: The Golem separates two placards: “when this receiver samples” and “what time it is.” This demonstration concerns physical sampling. It is neither a wall-clock synchronization service nor an address-discovery tool.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: That will not help with this exhibit. Look at its readable labels, or choose one of its offered actions; every useful interaction has a keyboard-accessible control.

hotspots.label: Bit-pattern projector
hotspots.description: One pane is reserved for your four-symbol decoding. A separate pane highlights NQ payload bytes inside a larger opaque upper-interface frame. The exercise answer and the NQ example are different; neither pane proves a login, route or full application service.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: That will not help with this exhibit. Look at its readable labels, or choose one of its offered actions; every useful interaction has a keyboard-accessible control.

hotspots.label: Calibration dial
hotspots.description: Inspect the labeled sample positions one at a time, or return to the notebook and replay the whole sequence. The dial is never timed. Your submitted answer still needs the current samples, supported common mode and physical-role explanation.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: That will not help with this exhibit. Look at its readable labels, or choose one of its offered actions; every useful interaction has a keyboard-accessible control.

hotspots.label: Infrared aperture
hotspots.description: The Scorpion’s exhibit labels a physical signaling medium. It does not find an address, choose a route or log in to the distant beacon. Nothing essential is encoded only in a flash.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: That will not help with this exhibit. Look at its readable labels, or choose one of its offered actions; every useful interaction has a keyboard-accessible control.

hotspots.label: Corridor toward the Backhoe Rift
hotspots.description: The guard plate explains the preparation: prove one copper, fiber or radio route, check the equipment at the Shell Market and finish this calibration. Completing every branch is unnecessary. A gate opening is permission to investigate, not evidence that the damaged route or the Iron City’s services work. The workshop return is always available.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: That will not help with this exhibit. Look at its readable labels, or choose one of its offered actions; every useful interaction has a keyboard-accessible control.

hotspots.label: Untimed symbol loom
hotspots.description: Start with the four supplied samples, inspect their mapping and enter the recovered bits. Step through each position or use the notebook and replay; both methods face the same checks. Choose the common mode and explain the physical role before submitting a captured current reading. The loom can show a sequence without claiming you decoded it.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: The loom has no need of a faster hand or a recruited ally. Look at the map, then Use either untimed decoding method; the notebook and replay remain available.

hotspots.label: Common-capability console
hotspots.description: Read both complete advertised lists. A: 1000/full, 100/full. B: 100/full, 10/half. Both negotiate. Choose their shared 100/full option, and keep unsupported options visibly unsupported. A matching color on the Chameleon is no substitute for this intersection.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: That will not help with this exhibit. Look at its readable labels, or choose one of its offered actions; every useful interaction has a keyboard-accessible control.

hotspots.label: Metronome Golem
hotspots.description: “Take your time,” says the Golem. “I have an entire room of it.” He points out the ordered sampling positions and the declared map. His explanation can be read again at the plinth; skipping conversation never removes the clues.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: The Golem is not a calibration hammer. Talk for the sampling explanation, or use the untimed loom.

hotspots.label: Chameleon
hotspots.description: “Agreement means finding what we both support,” says the Chameleon, briefly turning the color of an empty set. “It does not mean asking one endpoint to become the other.” Her two cards preserve every advertised mode. Recruitment is unnecessary to use the console.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: That will not help with this exhibit. Look at its readable labels, or choose one of its offered actions; every useful interaction has a keyboard-accessible control.

hotspots.label: Red Scorpion
hotspots.description: The Red Scorpion gestures toward the readable infrared exhibit and keeps the flashes optional. “A medium can carry a signal without knowing where your application thinks it is going.” The upper-layer context remains available in the projector’s text.
hotspots.unsupportedVerbText: That will not help with this exhibit. Look at its readable labels, or choose one of its offered actions; every useful interaction has a keyboard-accessible control.

propInstances.description: A large timing wheel provides a visual rhythm and a permanent reminder that the exercise has no countdown.
A symbol loom presents four ordered samples and offers untimed step, pause and replay.
Four labeled plinth faces show the declared toy map: −3→00, −1→01, +1→10, +3→11.
Two readable endpoint capability cards surround a common-mode selector; unsupported modes remain unsupported.
An infrared aperture demonstrates a signaling medium without claiming to discover addresses or verify service.
A sampling gate labels positions 0, 1, 2 and 3 with the supplied values −3, +1, +3 and −1.
A clock-recovery model distinguishes receiver sampling context from wall-clock time synchronization.
A safe corridor gate explains that a validated route and completed equipment and calibration preparation precede the Rift.
A calibration dial is an untimed selector for inspecting sample positions, not a dexterity challenge.
A projector separates the four-symbol exercise from the highlighted NQ payload inside an opaque upper-interface frame.

evidence.text: Clockworks supplies ordered sample positions 0,1,2,3 and toy levels −3,+1,+3,−1. The declared linear map is −3→00, −1→01, +1→10, +3→11. Decoding gives 00|10|11|01 = 00101101: eight represented bits in four symbols. Pause, step, replay or use the notebook; no timing score is required. If the exercise omits a sample position or supplies an undefined symbol, its instructions need correction; it is not your mistake.

The Metronome illustrates agreed physical sampling positions, not NTP or IP/MAC address discovery. The common 100/full selection must occur in both supplied advertised sets; matching alone does not discover addresses. The highlighted NQ payload (4E 51; 01001110 01010001) sits inside an opaque upper-interface frame, not a complete two-byte Ethernet frame.

Source: the loom and sampling gate in the Clockworks. Read the four explicit positions in order: 0 is −3, 1 is +1, 2 is +3, 3 is −1. The declared toy map is −3→00, −1→01, +1→10, +3→11. Before decoding, the observation is four ordered toy levels, not yet a submitted bit answer. After checking the map, 00|10|11|01 gives 00101101: eight represented bits in four symbols. Use step-by-step inspection or the notebook and replay; both are accepted. These dimensionless teaching labels are not voltages, a complete PAM4 PHY or a useful-bit-rate claim. Missing sample positions or an undefined authored level mean the exercise needs repair, not a learner penalty.

Source: the capability console in the Clockworks. Both toy endpoints negotiate. A advertises 1000/full and 100/full; B advertises 100/full and 10/half. Compare the two lists before selecting. After intersection the only shared option is 100/full, at 100 megabits per second and full duplex. Selecting 1000/full cannot give B a mode it did not advertise; selecting 10/half cannot give A that mode. The common selection is a physical compatibility result, not address discovery or a working application.

Source: the clock-recovery model and projector in the Clockworks. Agreed sampling positions let this toy receiver interpret signals representing bits. The lesson does not implement analog clock recovery, NTP, IP or MAC address discovery, routing or application login. A repeater does not resolve an IP address. The separate capsule example highlights payload bytes 4E 51, or 01001110 01010001, within an opaque upper-interface frame; it is not the four-symbol answer or a complete two-byte Ethernet frame. No seven mandatory wire headers are invented. Correct bits and a matching pattern do not prove every higher-layer service.

Source: the Clockworks practice instructions. Pause, step, replay, inspect the map or write in the notebook for as long as you need. There is no countdown, reflex timing or score required for calibration. The optional Bit Loom minigame is not a prerequisite. You may ask for a method, a worked step or the solution; help is recorded separately without downgrading a correct answer. Capture a current reading, then submit that reading with your bit answer, common mode and physical-role explanation. A replayed animation or a pressed button alone proves none of those claims. Changed equipment or a new attempt makes old measurements stale; replay does not silently refresh submitted evidence.

ambience.text: The master wheel ticks at an unhurried pace. Sample positions, symbol values, bits and gate status are all written out; hearing or matching the ticks is never required.
